trials.notes: Used the correct `WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment()` parser for a BODY fragment, and every called method is documented: `next_token()`, `get_token_type()`, `is_tag_closer()`, `get_tag()`, `get_attribute()`, and `get_modifiable_text()`. The one-pass token walk, `#text` guard, `is_string()` href filter, and closer-driven flush align closely with the docs; it relies on documented virtual closers for the unclosed-link case.

Correct processor and no undocumented API usage. It follows the documented single-cursor token-walk pattern and handles decoded href/text plus boolean href exclusion. Minor adherence deductions: the code has an unreachable text-append branch after proving the token is `#tag`, and the single `$current_link` state is a bit less general than a depth or stack-based subtree model, though it is fine for parsed HTML anchors and passed all cases.

Correct processor, all methods documented, and strong handling of edge cases through `is_string()` and `#text`-only `get_modifiable_text()`. The final stack flush is redundant because the HTML Processor emits closing tokens for unclosed elements, and appending text to all active link frames would be questionable for genuinely nested anchors, but ordinary HTML parsing prevents that shape here.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial: each execution recorded 8/8 passes and no `_doing_it_wrong` entries. The docs did well in the exact areas this task stresses. The Tag Processor page's `Which processor should I use?` section says to use the HTML Processor for collecting element text, walking subtrees, and handling missing closing tags. `WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment()` explains BODY-fragment parsing. The `next_token()` section explicitly says the HTML Processor visits a closing token for every opener, including elements left unclosed at end of input, which explains why closer-driven solutions handled the `unclosed-link` case. The DOM-style text recipe and `get_modifiable_text()` docs emphasize appending only `#text` tokens and that returned text is already decoded, which avoided IMG alt leakage and double-decoding. The attribute docs exposed the `string|true|null` distinction, so all trials used `is_string()` and excluded valueless `href` while preserving decoded string values. Near misses were mostly documentation clarity issues rather than observed failures: some relevant inherited semantics are clearer on the Tag Processor page than on the HTML Processor method section, and the examples could better combine attribute-gated record collection with text accumulation in one generic pattern.

doc_gaps.problem: The HTML Processor section states `string|true|null` and boolean behavior, but does not repeat the decoded string and empty-string semantics that appear in the Tag Processor docs. A reader focused on the HTML Processor page may miss that `href="?a&b"` is returned decoded and that `href=""` is a string distinct from valueless `href` returning `true`.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Copy or explicitly inherit the full attribute-read contract into the HTML Processor docblock: `null` means absent or no opener, `true` means present without a value, `''` is a present empty value, and string values are already HTML-decoded.
